name: Mercedes 722.6 5-speed TCU (EGS52)

read_methods.notes: Bench connection: supply, ground and K-line on C1 (ecupinouts); CAN is on the C2 connector (ATSG). OBD programming capability is not documented in the cited sources.

notes: External (body-mounted) TCU for the Mercedes 722.6 5-speed automatic, also used by Chrysler. Per ATSG, 1996-1999 units read the range switch on C1-25..28 while 2000+ units use CAN. The open-source ultimate_nag52 project is a drop-in replacement TCU for EGS51/52/53 cars. No OpenTune checksum applies.

pins.function: Diagnosis line to the data-link connector (K-line)

pins.note: Sources do not say whether this is switched; feed +12 V on the bench.
Solenoid feed - not needed to talk to the TCU on the bench.

bench.notes: +12 V to C1-29, ground C1-30, K-line C1-1. CAN-H/L are on C2 (pins labelled H and L) if your tool uses CAN.
bench.resistor_notes: For CAN on the bench a forum thread recommends terminating the bus (about 60 ohm across CAN-H/CAN-L).

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
